tb21_profile.skill: Infer an exact per-row text transformation by diffing input against expected output, then express it in a deliberately restricted editing language (vim normal-mode keystrokes and :s regexes) under a keystroke and runtime budget, byte-exact over a million rows
tb21_profile.domain: Vim/ex editing, regular-expression substitution, CSV line and field munging, byte-exact file output
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec constrained by a budget: reverse-engineer the rule, encode it minimally in an allowed-command subset, verified by byte-for-byte comparison

searches: tools.py search all "byte-for-byte|byte for byte|exactly match(es)? the expected|identical to the expected|diff -u? .*expected|expected_output" -n 30
tools.py search all "using only (bash|shell|awk|sed)|must be implemented in Bash|Do not use Python|only standard (shell|Unix) (utilities|tools)|Bash, Awk" -n 25
tools.py search all "million (rows|lines|records)|large file|streaming|memory-efficient|line by line|must complete within|time limit|performance constraint" -n 30
tools.py search tmax "records per second|throughput of at least|1,000,000|1 million|100MB|large CSV|process .* rows quickly|efficient enough" -n 22
tools.py search tmax "oracle.*(text|string|CSV|transform)|reverse[- ]engineer.*(transformation|format|rule)|match the oracle|bit-for-bit|replicate the (exact|legacy) (output|behaviou?r)" -n 22

TMax-15K.reason: Must deduce an unknown string transformation purely from input/output behaviour and reproduce it exactly — the diff-and-infer core of this task.
CSV transformation restricted to awk and coreutils with output that must match the requested format exactly; same restricted-DSL editing.
Deduce a character-substitution plus run-length transform by probing an oracle and produce bit-for-bit identical output.
Multi-stage CSV processing with Python and friends forbidden; forces expressing field edits in sed/awk one-liners.
Replicate a legacy per-line log-text canonicaliser exactly; line-in, line-out transformation with no tolerance for drift.
Reproduce a legacy tool's output bit-for-bit using only shell utilities, no new binary — restricted toolset plus byte-exactness.
Stream a large CSV, rewrite the text field of every row to an exact format, and stay memory-bounded; scale plus per-row edits.
Shell-only reimplementation that must be bit-exact against a hidden oracle under fuzzing; every transformation step must be faithful.
Stream a large CSV applying strict per-row rules and emit exactly the surviving rows; row-level filtering at scale.
Must handle a million lines of stdin efficiently; the throughput constraint that makes naive per-line editing time out.

Per-column statistics over generated data using only head/wc/awk with Python explicitly banned; restricted-tool column work.

Produce a file that exactly matches a reference rendering; only the exact-match discipline transfers.

Importing ragged CSV rows of differing widths; the uneven-row hazard of transforming a million-row CSV uniformly.

CSV field transformation restricted to awk and shell, with output that must match the required format exactly.
Probe an oracle to work out a character-substitution transform, then match it bit-for-bit on arbitrary input.
Pattern-match text with whitespace and digits and replace every occurrence in place across files; a substitution command in disguise.
Multi-step CSV pipeline with high-level languages banned, forcing terse sed/awk expressions over columns.
Reimplement a legacy per-line text canonicaliser whose output must match exactly, line in and line out.
Write one regular expression that satisfies a list of precise format rules and correctly splits a dataset.
Match a reference tool's output bit-for-bit using only shell utilities; restricted toolset plus byte-exact verification.
Stream a large CSV and rewrite each row's text field to an exact format without loading the file; per-row edits at scale.

notes: There is essentially no Vim in the pool: a search for vim/vimrc/:%s//normal!/sed -i across all 56k instructions returned twelve hits, of which the only vim-centric one is tw_17688 (compile Vim from source), whose skill transfer is nil — I deliberately left it out rather than let the domain word carry it. So the ranking is built on the three components the task actually decomposes into: (1) infer an exact transformation from examples and reproduce it byte-for-byte, where TMax's large oracle-reimplementation family is excellent; (2) express per-row CSV edits in a restricted language, where TMax's 'no Python, use awk/sed' family and TerminalWorld's in-place substitution tasks fit; (3) survive the scale/throughput budget, covered by the million-row streaming tasks. The shortlist was dominated by a false-positive class: 'macro' matched C preprocessor macros and 'macro payloads' in malware tasks, and 'large-scale text' matched generic ETL — none of those are in my lists. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench contribute text-rewriting libraries (flashtext, markdownify, docformatter, tomlkit, python-markdown) whose bugs are about exact character-level output; they lose on task_form as expected.
